findings.where: crates/io/src/legacy_pigment/mod.rs:172-184, 273, 284 (plane + encode_gray before container.write); crates/io/src/legacy_pigment/layers.rs:503-504 (place: encode before container.write); crates/io/src/legacy_pigment/container.rs:58-71 (decode_png keeps up to three copies)
findings.issue: Pixel memory is priced only in Container::write, after the importer has already read and encoded the whole plane. A saved channel or the selection (`plane`) is read whole (up to the 4 GiB entry budget, `max` is the plane size, not MAX_ENTRY_BYTES) and then encode_gray allocates pixels x bytes-per-sample of the document depth (x4 in a 32-bit document) before write() compares tile_storage_bytes with the 2 GiB pixel budget. A raster layer's PNG (decoded up to the 2 GiB pixel budget, kept as image + converted + to_vec) is expanded by encode() to 8 or 16 bytes per pixel in a 16- or 32-bit document before the same check. A tiny file therefore makes the importer allocate many GB for a document it then refuses as too large; past the machine's memory the process aborts (Rust's allocation failure is an abort, not an error), taking every other open document's unsaved work with it.
findings.scenario: Verified with the built pigment-cli (target/debug, the channel path is unchanged since L1). A 875 KB .pigment (python zipfile): document.json {app:'pigment', version:3, width:30000, height:30000, depth:32, layers:[], channels:[{id:'c1'}]} and channels/c1.bin = 900,000,000 bytes of 0xFF, deflated. `pigment-cli info` peaks at 4.3 GB RSS for 7.7 s and then says 'too large to open'; under `ulimit -v 3000000` it aborts with 'memory allocation of 3600000000 bytes failed' in layers::encode_gray <- channels_and_selection <- legacy_pigment::import. The same file at 60000 x 60000 (a 3.6 GB plane, still under the 4 GiB entry budget, about 3.5 MB on disk) needs 3.6 + 14.4 GB and is OOM-killed on a 16 GB machine. A 32-bit document with one 16000 x 16000 transparent PNG layer (996 KB file) peaks at 4.9 GB before the same refusal; at 23000 x 23000 it needs about 14 GB. Through File > Open, drag and drop, Open Recent, the command line or an agent's app.open the GUI process dies.
findings.test: In legacy_pigment/tests.rs: import_at with Budget { bytes: MAX_TOTAL_BYTES, pixels: 1 << 20 } on a 1000 x 1000, depth-32 document whose channels/c1.bin is a valid 1,000,000-byte plane (and, separately, whose raster layer is a 1000 x 1000 PNG). Expect IoError::Unsupported('too large') and assert the budget's `bytes` after the call is what document.json alone cost, i.e. the plane entry was never read (today the 1 MB plane is read and 4 MB encoded first). A second check with a counting #[global_allocator] in a dedicated test binary can assert peak allocation stays under 2x the file's size for the 875 KB file above.
findings.fix: Price before reading and encoding. In channels_and_selection, compute tile_storage_bytes(canvas, &mask_fmt) and return too_large when it exceeds container.pixel_budget before calling plane(); for the selection, do the same before plane(). In LayerReader::place (and in raster() before reading a deep plane), check tile_storage_bytes(rect, &self.fmt) <= pixel_budget before encode(). In mask(), check the mask rect at mask_fmt before encode_gray. Optionally drop the extra copy in decode_png (take the converted buffer instead of `.data().to_vec()`), and charge the decoded PNG against the budget while it lives.

findings.where: crates/io/src/legacy_pigment/smart.rs:177-189 (render: the engine path `continue`s without charging `budget`); crates/engine/src/cmd/smart_cmds/rendering.rs:177-208 + crates/engine/src/cmd/transform_cmds.rs:343-366 (the engine prices each placement alone against Memory Usage, default 8192 MB)
findings.issue: The fix for the reviewed smart-object OOM (c085534) priced only the fallback path. When the engine's renderer is installed (every real open path: jobs::import_options, file_cmds::open), smart::render hands each smart object to smart_cmds::refresh_layer and, if it returns true, moves on without charging the importer's 2 GiB pixel budget. The engine checks each placement on its own against Preferences > Performance > Memory Usage (DEFAULT_MEMORY_USAGE_MB = 8192, also the static default in pigment-cli/MCP where prefs may not be applied), and smart filters add stages of the same size. So one smart object may take up to 8 GiB plus its filter stages, and N instances sharing one tiny source (sourceRef) with transforms that differ (so the placed-stage cache does not share them) each keep their own cache: memory is N x up to 8 GiB, from a file of a few KB.
findings.scenario: A .pigment with smart/s.png = a 64 x 64 opaque PNG and 4 layers {type:'smart', id:'s'|..., sourceRef:'s', transform:[300,0,0,300,k,0]} with k = 0,1,2,3 (each placement 19200 x 19200 RGBA8 = 1.47 GB, under the engine's 8 GiB per-warp limit, and the importer never adds them up). Opening it allocates about 5.9 GB of caches; 12 such layers (a 2 KB document.json) need about 18 GB and the process is OOM-killed on a 16 GB machine, although the importer's own limit is 2 GiB. With one layer at scale 700 (44800 x 44800 x 4 = 8.03 GB < 8 GiB) a single smart object already takes 8 GB, plus one more stage per smart filter. Not run here: the built pigment-cli predates L3 (it has no smart-object import), so this is traced through the code.
findings.test: Engine test next to legacy_pigment_render::tests (where active_budget is 20 MB): a file with a 64 px PNG source and 40 instances at scale 35 with distinct x offsets (2240 x 2240 x 4 = 20 MB each, 800 MB in all) opened through a test-only importer budget of 256 MB (e.g. a #[cfg(test)] override of MAX_PIXEL_BYTES or an import_at entry point taking Budget). Assert that the sum of tile_storage_bytes of every sm.cache is <= 256 MB and that the import warnings name the instances left undrawn ('could not be drawn'). Today all 40 are drawn.
findings.fix: In smart::render, before calling the renderer, price the placement exactly as the fallback does (warp_output_size of the source rect by sm.transform x bpp with alpha; for a .pcraft source use its bounds) and skip with the 'could not be drawn' warning when it exceeds *budget; after a successful render charge the real cost (tile_storage_bytes of the cache's bounds, or the priced cost) to *budget. A cheap source-size probe is needed for that: read the PNG header (photocraft_codecs dimensions) or the .pcraft manifest size instead of decoding.

findings.where: crates/io/src/legacy_pigment/smart.rs:46 and 177-189 (Renderer = fn(&Document, &mut Layer) -> bool, no Interrupt; render() never calls ctl.check()); crates/engine/src/legacy_pigment_render.rs:17-19 -> crates/engine/src/cmd/smart_cmds/rendering.rs:411-416 (refresh_layer uses JobCtx::new(), never cancelled)
findings.issue: Drawing smart objects and their smart filters at open time cannot be cancelled. The import's Interrupt (the open job's Cancel, a closed tab) is not passed to smart::render, the render loop does not check it between smart objects, and the engine renders each one with a fresh JobCtx, so its per-filter ctx.check() never fires. filters.rs accepts up to 256 filters per smart object with large clamps (median and dust-and-scratches radius 500, gaussian/high-pass/unsharp radius 1000, box/motion blur 2000).
findings.scenario: A .pigment (a few KB) with one smart object whose 64 px PNG source is placed at scale 300 (19200 x 19200, within both budgets even after IMP-2's fix) and whose `filters` list holds 256 x {kind:'median', params:{radius:500}}. File > Open (or a drag and drop, Open Recent, the command line) starts the open job; it runs for hours at full CPU and Cancel does nothing, because the importer only checks ctl again after smart::render returns. Through the control channel (an agent's app.open -> open_automation_bytes, which imports on the UI thread) the whole window freezes with no way out but killing the app. A genuine 0.4 document with a large smart object and a few heavy filters shows the same: the open cannot be cancelled while its filters run.
findings.test: Engine test: an Interrupt whose cancel closure returns true once progress >= 0.8 (the importer reports 0.8 right before smart::render) opening a document with one smart object carrying 8 x gaussian-blur radius 1000; expect Err(IoError::Cancelled) within 1 s, and that the layer's renderer ran at most once. Today the import completes every filter and returns Ok.
findings.fix: Pass the interrupt through: make Renderer fn(&Document, &mut Layer, &Interrupt) -> Result<bool, Cancelled> (the engine side builds a JobCtx whose check() asks the Interrupt, or calls refresh_layer_in with such a ctx), check ctl before each smart object in smart::render, and propagate Cancelled out of import as IoError::Cancelled (as prepare_within already does).

findings.where: crates/ui-egui/src/dialogs/legacy_save_prompt.rs:31-33 (still_legacy reads the whole file); called from intercept (line 43) on the UI thread by every File > Save (app/files.rs:316-321)
findings.issue: Review item 7, confirmed and worth fixing for 0.5.0. came_from_legacy(doc) stays true for good (the import report is saved in the native format, and copied by Duplicate and by smart-object contents opened with Edit Contents), so every later File > Save of such a document reads its whole file into memory on the UI thread just to look at the ZIP directory. The native format is also a ZIP, so nothing short-circuits it. A 1 GB document freezes the window for the read and holds 1 GB extra at each Ctrl+S, on top of the background save's own snapshot.
findings.scenario: Open a Pigment 0.4 file, Save (answer Save in the prompt), keep working: the file is now native (e.g. 800 MB of tiles). Each later Ctrl+S calls still_legacy -> std::fs::read(800 MB) -> is_legacy, which returns false, before the save starts. Only ticking 'Don't show again' avoids it (dismissed() is checked first).
findings.test: ui-egui unit test with a Services::file_stamp/read counter is awkward for std::fs; instead test still_legacy directly: write a 64 MB native .pigment (or a ZIP with a large stored entry) to a temp dir and assert still_legacy returns false while reading at most the tail (e.g. by passing a File and counting bytes read through a wrapper reader), and that it still returns true for v3-groups.pigment.
findings.fix: Read only the ZIP directory: open the file and hand a std::fs::File to zip::ZipArchive::new (it seeks to the end record and reads only the central directory), or read the last 64 KiB + the central directory it points to; check for document.json and the absence of manifest.json as brand::is_legacy_pigment does (a brand::is_legacy_pigment_reader taking Read + Seek keeps the rule in one place). Cheaper still: remember (doc, path, disk stamp) once a save to that path succeeded and skip the check while the stamp is unchanged.

findings.where: crates/ui-egui/src/dialogs/legacy_save_prompt.rs:80-89 (confirm never releases the close prompt); crates/ui-egui/src/dialogs/discard_ui.rs:222-256 (save() returns false while the legacy prompt is pending) and 264-272 (saved_document)
findings.issue: Review item 6, narrowed. With the default desktop settings the save started by the legacy prompt's Save runs as a background job, and jobs_ui::finish_save calls discard_ui::saved_document, which moves the close/quit prompt on: no second Save is needed there. With inline saves (PHOTOCRAFT_INLINE_JOBS set, which the ui-egui tests use too) write_document writes synchronously, nothing calls saved_document, and the close prompt stays up asking about a document that is already saved; the user must press Save again (which writes again, since intercept no longer asks).
findings.scenario: PHOTOCRAFT_INLINE_JOBS=1 pigment; open a 0.4 file, change it, File > Close (or quit), choose Save: the legacy prompt opens; choose Save there: the file is written and the document is clean, but the close prompt still asks; Save again writes the file a second time and only then closes.
findings.test: In legacy_save_prompt_tests.rs: with background_jobs = false, start file.close on a dirty legacy document, answer Save in the close prompt, confirm the legacy prompt with Save; assert app.discard is None and the document is closed after the next frame (today the prompt is still there).
findings.fix: Not needed for the default 0.5.0 desktop path. If fixed: let confirm return the save result to save_prompt_confirm's caller, which has the egui Context (or park the DocId in app state) and call discard_ui::saved_document(app, ctx, doc) when the write was synchronous (result without "pending"), as write_answered_save does. The upstream disk-change prompt has the same gap.

findings.issue: The first Save over a 0.4 file overwrites the only copy of what the import left out, and the prompt does not say so. Smart filters with no counterpart, type settings PhotoCraft lacks, a stroke on a pattern-filled shape, smart objects nested more than 8 deep and similar items are dropped at import (SkippedNonessential in the report), not kept raw; Save (the default button) then replaces the 0.4 file with a native one that cannot get them back. The prompt only says Pigment 0.4 will no longer open the file.
findings.scenario: A 0.4 document with a smart object whose filters include a kind filters.rs does not map, or a type layer with lists or tab stops: it opens with those reported in the warnings (which the user may have dismissed). Later Ctrl+S, Enter on the default Save: the 0.4 file is overwritten and the filters and type settings are gone; with 'Don't show again' ticked earlier, no question at all.
findings.test: legacy_save_prompt_tests: open a fixture whose report has a SkippedNonessential entry (e.g. v3 smart filters with an unmapped kind) and assert the prompt's message mentions that parts were left out and that its default choice is Save As; for a fixture with only NativeApproximation entries the message stays as today.
findings.fix: When the document's import report has entries with ConversionDisposition::SkippedNonessential, add a line to the prompt ('Some parts of this document were left out when it opened; saving over the file loses them for good.') and make Save As the default choice ('choice': 'saveAs'); optionally ignore 'Don't show again' for such documents.

checked: Read docs/FORK.md and PKG-port-L1/L2/L3/review-L and PKG-ai-final's scope. Examined: container.rs (ZIP limits, entry/byte budget, nested Budget sharing, decode_png limits), mod.rs (size/mode/depth, duotone and colour table, channels and selection, guides, paths, light, profile, report dispositions, came_from_legacy, import_at), layers.rs (tree depth and node limits, offsets, raster/deep planes, masks, links, blending/Blend If, shape cache pricing, fill tiles), smart.rs (sourceRef sharing, nesting limit, nested budget, fallback pricing), text.rs (UTF-16 to UTF-8 runs incl. surrogate splits, paragraph lengths, matrix limits, empty text), filters.rs (clamps, adjustment params), adjust.rs curve parsing and monotone spline (sorted, deduplicated, n>=2; drawn tables must be 256), LUT axis indexing, info.rs (XML escaping, EXIF date slicing on char boundaries), legacy_pigment_render.rs, legacy_save_prompt.rs and its hooks in app/files.rs, menus/invoke.rs file.save, dialogs.rs routing, replay_save (played Save does not ask), discard_ui interplay, jobs_ui background saves, io lib.rs routing/preflight. Ran the built pigment-cli (L1-era build; channel path unchanged): legacy fixtures open under misleading names (.pdf .svg .ai .jpg .psd) by content; the hostile channel file and the hostile 32-bit PNG layer reproduce IMP-1 (4.3 GB and 4.9 GB peak, abort under a 3 GB limit). Sound: entry-count and expanded-byte limits, document.json size, group depth (serde's 128 limit), MAX_NODES, offsets and Rect arithmetic in i32, MAX_SIDE, curve/LUT indexing, byte_runs and paragraph splitting, hex colour parsing, XMP escaping, nesting depth 8 with shared byte budget, shape caches priced before render, the fallback smart placement priced (c085534), played Save and engine file.save bypass the prompt as documented, the prompt never asks twice once the file is native, Cancel/Save As/Don't show again route correctly, opening adds no history step. Not re-reported: review items 4, 5 (upstream text/vector performance) and 8 (by design), and PKG-ai-final's items (none judged blocking).
